source_basis.title: Caracterizacion del peligro por movimiento de masa debido a lluvias extremas en la quebrada Malanche, distrito de Punta Hermosa

event_reference.event_context: SENAMHI report states that the 14 March 2023 Malanche/Punta Hermosa event required an extreme reconstructed scenario above the evaluated 500-year return-period scenario to reproduce comparable effects.

exposure_reference.report_finding: Pampacta and Santa Rosa de Punta Hermosa are broadly affected in simulated return-period scenarios; the urban area near the beach requires an extreme reconstructed event to reproduce 2023-type effects.

soil_and_sediment_reference.interpretation: decreasing cohesion with depth can facilitate mass movement after erosion of the upper layer

known_limitations: No original DTM, DSM, orthophoto, point cloud, HEC-HMS project or HEC-RAS project is available to IRFEN.
No direct water-flow or sediment measurements were available to validate the SENAMHI simulations.
The approximately 302.6 m3/s 2023 reconstruction is modelled, not an observed gauged discharge.
The Antioquia rainfall station is a representative regional station selected by SENAMHI and is not a local Malanche rain gauge.
Short-duration IDF values in the study were estimated indirectly because pluviograph intensity records were unavailable or not supplied.
The official report can close the research validation reference case but cannot justify operational thresholds, production promotion or public alerting.

allowed: independent comparison of IRFEN basin morphometry against published SENAMHI values
independent comparison of satellite rainfall descriptors against the Antioquia reference series and published frequency values
event/non-event research testing using 2023 as an independently documented activation case
comparison of IRFEN susceptibility and exposure outputs against published SENAMHI maps and sectors
testing whether rainfall duration plus intensity plus morphology improves activation discrimination
forbidden: calibrating IRFEN geometry to force agreement with SENAMHI published morphometry
treating modelled discharge as an observed outcome
deriving production alert thresholds directly from the SENAMHI return-period table
claiming raw 3 m terrain validation without the original terrain products
